title: Annotatio III §.VI: Lanfranc and doctors pierce him — Leo IX (1049) & Nicholas II (1059): judgment, prison, recantation
pass_a_gloss: On that account, pierced by the pens of private as well as public Doctors, especially Lanfranc of Canterbury, or their standard-bearer, he was by Popes Leo IX in the year 1049 and Nicholas II in the year 1059 not only called into judgment, but also committed to prison and driven to a recantation conceived in these words.
pass_b_english: Private and public doctors — Lanfranc of Canterbury foremost — pierce him with their pens.
Leo IX (1049) and Nicholas II (1059) haul him to judgment, prison, and a forced recantation.
source_text: Ob id, privatorum pariter atque publicorum Doctorum cumprimis Lanfranci Cantuariensis, seu istorum Antesignani, calamis confossus, à Papis Leone IX. anno 1049. & Nicolao II. anno 1059. non solum in judicium vocatus, sed & carceri mancipatus & ad recantationem his conceptam verbis adactus.
